subject: Behavioral Economics
title: Scope Insensitivity
description: Learn Scope Insensitivity in one minute.

hook.text: People donate the same amount to save 2,000 birds as to save 200,000 birds. The number barely registers.

buildup.text: Kahneman found our emotional response doesn't scale with magnitude. One victim moves us; millions don't.

discovery.text: Scope insensitivity: our feelings respond to the image, not the number. One starving child beats a statistic.

twist.text: Stalin allegedly said one death is a tragedy, a million is a statistic. Our brains actually work that way.

climax.text: To think proportionally, convert big numbers to rates or comparisons you can feel viscerally.

punchline.text: Our hearts can't count past one.

quiz.question: What does scope insensitivity cause?
options: We donate more as the problem grows larger
Our emotional response doesn't scale with the size of the problem
We always respond proportionally to numbers

details.summary: Scope insensitivity is the failure to scale emotional and economic responses proportionally to the size of a problem. People are willing to pay almost the same to save 2,000 birds as to save 200,000 birds because the emotional response does not scale with magnitude.
details.whyItMatters: Scope insensitivity distorts charitable giving, environmental policy, and risk assessment. Society allocates resources based on emotional impact rather than the magnitude of the problem, leading to disproportionate responses to small vivid issues.
takeaways: Emotional responses do not scale proportionally with problem magnitude
Willingness to pay barely increases with the number of lives or items at stake
Scope insensitivity explains why small vivid problems attract more resources than large diffuse ones

faq.question: Why are people willing to pay nearly the same amount to save 2,000 or 200,000 birds?
faq.answer: The emotional image of a bird in distress does not change with the number. People respond to the prototype, the single suffering bird, and scale the image rather than the number. The emotional system generates a response to the category, not the quantity.

faq.question: How does scope insensitivity affect policy and charitable decisions?
faq.answer: Resources flow to emotionally vivid causes rather than numerically larger ones. A dramatic rescue of one child receives more donations than a program saving thousands. Policy responds to emotional resonance rather than magnitude of impact.
